title.zh: 卷七十六 循吏列傳
title.raw: 卷七十六 循吏列傳 Volume 76: Biographies of Upright Officials

title.zh: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝
title.raw: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Hui

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 初，光武長于民間，頗達情僞，見稼穡艱難，百姓病害，至天下已定，務用安靜，解王莽之繁密，還漢世之輕法。
value.en: Emperor Guangwu had been raised among ordinary folk, so he grasped what was real and what was not, and he had watched tillers suffer and the people sicken. Once the empire was his, he pursued calm government: he loosened Wang Mang’s suffocating code and brought back the Han tradition of relatively mild punishments.
value.literal: Earlier, Guangwu had grown up among the common people and was fairly versed in true and false; he had seen the hardship of farming and the ills of the people. When the realm was finally settled, he strove for quiet rule, undid Wang Mang’s tangled severity, and restored the Han era’s lighter laws.

value.zh: 身衣大練，色無重綵，耳不聽鄭、衛之音，手不持珠玉之玩，宫房無私爱，左右無偏恩。
value.en: He dressed in single layers of homespun, shunned gaudy dyes, shut out the licentious airs of Zheng and Wei, and kept his hands from jeweled playthings. He showed no private infatuation in the harem and no uneven favor to attendants.
value.literal: He personally wore thick plain silk; his garb held no doubled colors. His ears did not listen to the music of Zheng and Wei; his hands did not hold jade and pearl trinkets. The inner palace had no private favorites; those at his side received no lopsided grace.

value.zh: 建武十三年，異國有獻名馬者，日行千里，又進寶劒，賈兼百金，詔以馬駕鼓車，劒賜騎士。
value.en: In 37 a tributary state sent a thousand-li stallion and a blade worth a hundred catties of gold; the court hitched the horse to the ritual drum cart and gave the sword to a cavalryman instead of hoarding both.
value.literal: In the thirteenth Jianwu year, a foreign land presented a famous horse that could travel a thousand in a day; it also offered a precious sword worth a hundredweight of gold. An edict used the horse to pull the drum cart and bestowed the sword on a horseman.

value.zh: 損上林池籞之官，廢騁望弋獵之事。
value.en: He cut keepers of the imperial parks and put an end to pleasure hunts and hawking.
value.literal: He reduced the posts for Shanglin’s pools and preserves and abolished the business of coursing, gazing, and fowling for sport.

value.zh: 其以手迹賜方國者，皆一札十行，細書成文。
value.en: Letters to regional rulers were compact—one slip, ten lines, in his own tight hand.
value.literal: Those to whom he granted his own hand to vassal states all received a single tablet of ten lines, fine script forming the text.

value.zh: 勤約之風，行于上下。
value.en: Thrift and restraint ran from the throne to the clerks.
value.literal: Diligent frugality’s wind ran through high and low.

value.zh: 數引公卿郎將，列于禁坐。
value.en: He regularly called nobles, ministers, and generals to sit in the privy audience.
value.literal: He often summoned ministers, counselors, and generals, arraying them in the inner seat.

value.zh: 廣求民瘼，觀納風謠。
value.en: He asked after popular hardship and listened to local ballads and complaints.
value.literal: He broadly sought the people’s ailments and looked to take in the songs and laments of custom.

value.zh: 故能内外匪懈，百姓寬息。
value.en: So court and countryside stayed alert in duty, while commoners could breathe again.
value.literal: Therefore inside and outside none slacked; the common people were relaxed and at rest.

value.zh: 自臨宰邦邑者，競能其官。
value.en: Local magistrates, for their part, rivaled one another in competence.
value.literal: As for those who personally governed districts and cities, vied in fulfilling their office.

value.zh: 若杜詩守南陽，號爲“杜母”，任延、錫光移變邊俗，斯其績用之最章章者也。
value.en: Du Shi in Nanyang was nicknamed the “Nourishing Mother”; Ren Yan and Xi Guang transformed borderlands—their records stand out clearest among model officials.
value.literal: Such as Du Shi guarding Nanyang, called “Mother Du”; Ren Yan and Xi Guang remade frontier custom—these are the most shining examples of their achievement and ability.

value.zh: 又第五倫、宋均之徒，亦足有可稱談。
value.en: The likes of Di Lun and Song Jun likewise deserve a word.
value.literal: Also men like Di Lun and Song Jun are enough to merit mention in discussion.

value.zh: 然建武、永平之間，吏事刻深，亟以謠言單辭，轉易守長。
value.en: Still, in the Jianwu–Yongping years governance turned harsh: one whisper or isolated accusation could cost a magistrate his post.
value.literal: Yet between Jianwu and Yongping, official business was severe and cutting; on slight rumor or single testimony, magistrates were often replaced.

value.zh: 故朱浮數上諫書，箴切峻政，鍾離意等亦規諷殷勤，以長者爲言，而不能得也。
value.en: Zhu Fu repeatedly protested the severity; Zhongli Yi and others pressed the same in careful language—useless against the trend.
value.literal: Therefore Zhu Fu several times presented remonstrance, needling the harsh government; Zhongli Yi and others also earnestly counseled in oblique remonstrance, pleading the example of the elder sort—yet they could not prevail.

value.zh: 所以中興之美，蓋未盡焉。
value.en: The “restored golden age” therefore remains imperfect.
value.literal: So the beauty of the restoration is probably not complete.

value.zh: 自章、和以後，其有善績者，徃徃不絕。
value.en: After the Zhangde and Yonghe reigns, capable magistrates kept appearing.
value.literal: From Zhang and He onward, those with good records have never ceased to appear.

value.zh: 如魯恭、吳祐、劉寬及潁川四長，並以仁信篤誠，使人不欺；
value.en: Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan, and the Yingchuan quartet ruled so honestly that people stopped lying to one another.
value.literal: Such as Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan, and the “four elders” of Yingchuan—all by benevolence, trust, and earnest good faith made men cease to deceive one another.

value.zh: 王堂、陳寵委任賢良，而職事自理：斯皆可以感物而行化也。
value.en: Wang Tang and Chen Chong delegated to talent and let affairs run themselves—they too transformed their jurisdictions.
value.literal: Wang Tang and Chen Chong entrusted office to worthy men, and business ordered itself—these too could move things and carry transformation.

value.zh: 邊鳳、延篤先後爲京兆尹，時人以辈前世趙、張。
value.en: Bian Feng and Yan Du, one after the other as governors of the capital, were likened to the legendary Zhao and Zhang of old.
value.literal: Bian Feng and Yan Du successively served as metropolitan governor; men of the age bracketed them with the Zhao and Zhang of earlier generations.

value.zh: 又王渙、任峻之爲洛陽令，明發姦伏，吏端禁止，然導德劉禮，有所未充，亦一時之良能也。
value.en: Wang Huan and Ren Jun as Luoyang magistrates exposed crime and kept clerks honest; moral instruction through ritual still fell short of the ideal, yet they ranked among the best of their time.
value.literal: Further Wang Huan and Ren Jun as magistrates of Luoyang laid bare hidden villainy; clerks stood straight and prohibitions held—yet in guiding virtue through ritual propriety something still fell short; still they were capable officers of their day.

value.zh: 今綴集殊聞顯迹，以爲《循吏篇》云。
value.en: What follows gathers notable deeds into the chapter "Chapter on Upright Officials" (the Xunli pian).
value.literal: Now I string together unusual hearings and shining deeds to form this chapter titled "Chapter on Upright Officials" (Xunli pian).

value.zh: 和帝時，稍遷桂陽太守。
value.en: Under Emperor He he rose to Guiyang governor.
value.literal: Under Emperor He he was gradually promoted governor of Guiyang.

value.zh: 郡濱南州，風俗脆薄，不識學義。
value.en: Southern Guiyang was shallow in learning.
value.literal: The commandery bordered the southern provinces—custom flimsy and thin—not knowing study and righteousness.

value.zh: 荆爲設丧纪婚姻制度，使知禮禁。
value.en: He codified funerals and weddings.
value.literal: Jing established mourning and marriage regulations—letting them know ritual prohibitions.

value.zh: 嘗行春到耒陽縣，人有蒋均者，兄弟爭財，互相言訟。
value.en: At Leiyang the Jiang brothers sued over inheritance.
value.literal: Once on spring circuit he reached Leiyang county—a man Jiang Jun—brothers quarreling over property—mutually sued.

value.zh: 荆對之嘆曰：“吾荷國重任，而教化不行，咎在太守。”
value.en: He blamed his own teaching for their quarrel.
value.literal: Jing sighed at them: "I bear the state's heavy charge—yet transformation does not proceed—the fault lies with the governor."

value.zh: 乃顾使吏上書陳狀，乞詣廷尉。
value.en: He ordered a report draft requesting his own impeachment.
value.literal: Thereupon turned ordering clerks memorialize status—begging to go to the minister of justice.

value.zh: 均兄弟感悔，各求受罪。
value.en: The brothers begged punishment instead.
value.literal: Jun brothers felt shame—each sought punishment.

value.zh: 在事十二年，父老稱歌。
value.en: Twelve years brought folk songs.
value.literal: Twelve years in office—elders sang praise.

value.zh: 以病自上，征拜諫議大夫，卒于官。
value.en: He retired reporting illness, became remonstrance counselor, died there.
value.literal: Illness submitted upward—summoned remonstrance counselor—died in office.

value.zh: 桂陽人爲立廟树碑。
value.en: Guiyang built him temple and stone.
value.literal: Guiyang people raised temple and stele.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 三月辛卯，誅太傅楊駿，駿弟衛將軍珧，太子太保濟，中護軍張劭，散騎常侍段廣、楊邈，左將軍劉預，河南尹李斌，中書令蔣俊，東夷校尉文淑，尚書武茂，皆夷三族。
value.en: In the third month Yang Jun and his entire faction were put to death: his brother Yang Yao, Yang Ji, Zhang Shao, Duan Guang, Yang Miao, Liu Yu, Li Bin, Jiang Jun, Wen Shu, and Wu Mao, with every branch of their families extirpated.
value.literal: In the third month, on the xinmao day, Grand Tutor Yang Jun was executed; Jun’s younger brother General of the Guards Yang Yao, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yang Ji, Central Protector of the Army Zhang Shao, Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary Duan Guang and Yang Miao, General of the Left Liu Yu, Intendant of Henan Li Bin, Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jun, Colonel of Eastern Yi Tribes Wen Shu, and Minister Wu Mao—all were exterminated to the third degree of kin.

value.zh: 壬辰，大赦，改元。
value.en: A general amnesty followed, and the reign title was changed again.
value.literal: On the renchen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

value.zh: 賈后矯詔廢皇太后爲庶人，徙于金墉城，告于天地宗廟。
value.en: Empress Jia forged an edict that stripped the empress dowager of her title, confined her in the Jinyong fortress, and had the act proclaimed to Heaven, Earth, and the imperial shrines.
value.literal: Empress Jia forged an edict deposing the empress dowager to commoner status, transferring her to the Jinyong Fortress, and reported it to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

value.zh: 誅太后母龐氏。
value.en: The dowager’s mother, Lady Pang, was executed.
value.literal: The empress dowager’s mother, the Lady Pang, was executed.

value.zh: 壬寅，徵大司馬、汝南王亮爲太宰，與太保衛瓘輔政。
value.en: Prince Liang of Runan was recalled from the grand marshal’s post to serve as grand steward alongside Grand Guardian Wei Guan as coregent.
value.literal: On the renyin day, Grand Marshal, Prince Liang of Runan, was summoned to be grand steward, and together with Grand Guardian Wei Guan assisted the government.

value.zh: 以秦王柬爲大將軍，東平王楙爲撫軍大將軍，鎮南將軍、楚王瑋爲衛將軍，領北軍中候，下邳王晃爲尚書令，東安公繇爲尚書左僕射，進封東安王。
value.en: Prince Jian of Qin took the supreme military command; Prince Mao of Dongping became general who soothes the army; Prince Wei of Chu became general of the guards and colonel of the northern camp; Prince Huang of Xiapi headed the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an became its senior deputy and was raised to prince of Dong’an.
value.literal: Prince Jian of Qin was made general-in-chief; Prince Mao of Dongping was made general-in-chief who soothes the army; General Who Guards the South, Prince Wei of Chu, was made general of the guards, heading the colonel of the northern armies; Prince Huang of Xiapi was made director of the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an was made left vice director of the secretariat and advanced in enfeoffment to prince of Dong’an.

value.zh: 督將侯者千八十一人。
value.en: One thousand eighty-one officers of commander rank or above were ennobled as marquises.
value.literal: Supervisors and generals who were marquises numbered one thousand eighty-one persons.

value.zh: 庚戌，免東安王繇及東平王楙，繇徙帶方。
value.en: Princes Yao and Mao were stripped of their posts, and Yao was banished to Daifang on the Korean frontier.
value.literal: On the gengxu day, Prince Yao of Dong’an and Prince Mao of Dongping were dismissed from office; Yao was transferred to Daifang.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。
value.en: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.
value.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

value.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」
value.en: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
value.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

value.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」
value.en: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
value.literal: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"

value.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。
value.en: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
value.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.

value.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。
value.en: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.
value.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.

value.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。
value.en: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.
value.literal: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.

value.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。
value.en: He thrashed servants himself.
value.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.

value.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。
value.en: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.
value.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.

value.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
value.en: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.
value.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.

value.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。
value.en: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.
value.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.

value.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。
value.en: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.
value.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.

value.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。
value.en: The Eastern Palace normally received five hundred thousand cash a month for all its expenses; he habitually drew two months in advance to provide for his favorites.
value.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.

value.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。
value.en: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.
value.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.

value.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。
value.en: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
value.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.

value.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。
value.en: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.
value.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.

value.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
value.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
value.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

value.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
value.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

value.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
value.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
value.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

value.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
value.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
value.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

value.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
value.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
value.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

value.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: Or I will finish you.
value.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
value.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
value.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

value.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
value.en: Or I will kill her myself.
value.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

value.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
value.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
value.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
value.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
value.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

value.zh: 要疏如律令。」
value.en: So commands the spell.'
value.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
value.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
value.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

value.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
value.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
value.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
value.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
value.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
value.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

value.zh: 議至日西不決。
value.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
value.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

value.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
value.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
value.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

value.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
value.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
value.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

value.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
value.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
value.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

value.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
value.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
value.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

value.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
value.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
value.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
value.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
value.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

value.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
value.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
value.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

value.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
value.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

value.zh: 南風，后名；
value.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
value.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
value.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
value.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
